Community Emergency Response Team (CERT) — Fremont Fire Department

The Fremont Fire Department CERT program is a free training program for Fremont residents age 18 and older. Participants learn to prepare for and prevent emergencies at home and gain hands-on disaster skills to help others. Graduates may elect to become CERT volunteers affiliated with the Fire Department. In a major disaster such as an earthquake, CERT volunteers organize into neighborhood-based teams, recognize and report the most serious incidents, and use life-saving skills to help neighbors — a lifeline between families and the City's emergency responders.

CERT Basic Training is a 20-hour curriculum: six class sessions of about three hours plus a final exercise simulating a major earthquake scenario (size-up, small fire suppression, interior search, triage and treatment, extricating trapped victims, final exam). Sessions cover: earthquake awareness and hazard mitigation; shutting off natural gas, water, and electrical utilities; fire types and extinguisher use; hazardous materials awareness; airway opening, bleeding control, and S.T.A.R.T. triage; head-to-toe assessment and disaster psychology; light search and rescue including building marking systems and lifting; and CERT organization under the Incident Command System. The program follows FEMA's national CERT curriculum; the participant manual is available in Chinese and Spanish. Contact: CERT@fremont.gov, (510) 494-4244. Winter 2027 CERT Basic Training runs 02/18/2027–03/07/2027.

Fremont is divided into six CERT Areas with designated staging areas at fire stations: North — Area A: Fire Station 1, 4200 Mowry Ave.; Area B: Fire Station 9, 39609 Stevenson Pl.; Area C: Fire Station 10, 5001 Deep Creek Rd. South — Area D: Fire Station 3, 40700 Chapel Way; Area E: Fire Station 4, 1000 Pine St.; Area F: Fire Station 5, 55 Hackamore Ln.
